one_month_reasoning: The window runs to the Oct 30 close (Nov 1 is a Sunday). Two scheduled events fall inside it. (1) Q3 2026 earnings, expected Wed Oct 21 after the close (Nasdaq/Zacks 'expected'; TI reported on Wednesdays in April and July). Consensus is Q3 $2.42 and Q4 $2.28 on LSEG (Zacks $2.39 / $2.18), against a $2.23-2.57 guide. (2) The $1.52 dividend goes ex on Oct 30 (record Oct 30 under T+1), which takes about $1.52 off the final close mechanically. My lane's evidence points to a solid print: brokers report TI enforcing new pricing on open POs, Avnet's June quarter was +50% y/y with book-to-bill above 1, and channel inventory is lean. Against that, the ECIA distributor sentiment index fell from 154.1 (June) to 136.7 (August), and participants expect growth to peak in Q3. TI's own lead times are only 'a couple of weeks' above a sub-13-week baseline, so a strong Q4 guide may already be priced (July's beat-and-raise produced a ~19% drawdown). I therefore centre the distribution at spot less the dividend plus about +0.3% drift for a likely beat (centre ~$293.3, roughly flat) with a 1-month sigma of 12.5%: 42%/3.5 = 12% plus an earnings-day premium. P(>= $293.80) is 0.49.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: horizon NTM EPS of $10.95 (0.25 x CY27 $10.10 + 0.75 x CY28 $11.6 = $11.2, less ~$0.25 GAAP SLAB amortization net of deal earnings) x 23.5x (a ~12% premium to the 21.0x peer median of CY27 P/E, below ADI's 25.0x) = $257. 40% FCF yield: CY28 FCF/share ~$11.0 ex-CHIPS at 4.0% = $275, plus ~$1 of CHIPS receivable still to be collected after the horizon = $276. The blend is about $265, ~10% below spot.

inputs_detail.derivation: LSEG/Yahoo is the broader panel with recent upward revisions. Zacks has CY27 $9.84 (13) with no recent revisions and CY28 $11.59.

0.25 x $10.10 + 0.75 x $11.6 = $11.2. I dropped my round-1 +3.5% pricing uplift: the 28-analyst consensus already absorbed 22-24 upward revisions in 30 days, and TI's own lead times are only modestly extended (Portrait), so the uplift was likely double-counting.

About $7.3B net cash outlay (33.4M shares x $231 less ~$0.4B SLAB cash) funded by cash and a $5B term loan. After-tax financing cost is ~$0.30/share against SLAB NOPAT plus early synergies of roughly the same size, so it is ~neutral before purchase amortization. Intangible amortization takes off ~$0.2-0.3. TI calls it accretive only excluding transaction-related costs.
913.2M basic and 920M diluted at Q2. Buybacks are slow while cash goes to the dividend and SLAB, so I use ~915M rather than my round-1 905M.

The 10-peer CY27 P/E median is 21.0x (range 14.6x-47.6x). The 8 core broad-line names have a median of 19.8x, and the 5 US core names have an NTM median of 22.1x. ADI, the closest comp, is at 25.0x CY27 and 25.9x NTM. 23.5x is inside the range and ~12% above the median. See comps_summary for why that premium is persistent and why it is not larger.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: CY28 FCF/share ~$11.0 ex-CHIPS / 4.0% = $275, plus ~$1.1/share of CHIPS incentives collected after the horizon

inputs_detail.derivation: CY28 EPS ~$11.6 + D&A ~$2.85/share (~$2.6B, rising with Sherman/Lehi ramps from TTM ~$2.1B) - capex ~$2.75-3.0/share ($2.5-2.75B, after the 2026 $2-3B plan) - working capital ~$0.45 = ~$11.2. Round down for capex uncertainty. TTM FCF on TI's definition is $6.53B including $1.18B CHIPS, or $5.36B excluding it.

inputs_detail.value: $2.16B on balance sheet; ~$1.0B (~$1.1/share) assumed to arrive after Oct 2027
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q: $1,005M current + $1,158M long-term. The current portion should arrive before the horizon (already in the cash that funds SLAB). I add the long-term portion as a one-off per-share value, not capitalized as recurring FCF.

Consistent with the 23.5x P/E leg: FCF/share ~= EPS by 2028, and TI's policy is to return ~100% of FCF. My round-1 3.75% (26.7x) implied a larger premium than I can justify against the 21x peer median, so I raise it to 4.0%.

bear.story: The 2026 shortage proves partly to be double-ordering and auto restocking (TI acknowledged auto pull-in in July; ECIA sentiment already rolled over from its June peak). Lead times peak in H1 2027, distributors cut orders, and CY28 EPS is revised to ~$9.5. The multiple falls to ~20.5x, the peer median, with the premium gone. SLAB adds leverage (~1x EBITDA) at the wrong time. About $195.

base.story: The upcycle runs through mid-2027 with EPS near the $10.10 / $11.6 consensus. Pricing gains hold but growth decelerates from its Q3 2026 peak, so the multiple compresses from ~31x NTM toward ~25x on ~$11.2 horizon EPS, about $280-285, plus the $6.08 dividend.

bull.story: Pricing on open POs and 300mm cost advantage push operating margin toward the prior ~50% peak. Data-center power and industrial carry demand into 2028, CY28 EPS reaches ~$13, and the market pays ~30x for a capex-light FCF ramp plus SLAB synergies. About $390.

comps_summary.peer_range: Basis: CY2027 calendarized consensus P/E (Zacks for US names, MarketScreener for IFX/Renesas/Melexis, all on 2026-10-02 closes; stockanalysis 'Forward PE' not used). Range 14.6x (NXPI) to 47.6x (MPWR); median of 10 is 21.0x. Core 8 broad-line analog/MCU/auto names (ex MPWR, ALGM): median 19.8x, range 14.6x-25.0x. US core NTM P/E (next four quarters ex the reporting quarter): ADI 25.9x, MCHP 22.1x, NXPI 15.2x, ON 20.2x, STM 27.7x, median 22.1x. Forward EV/EBITDA median 12.4x (range 8.1x-54.3x) on a MIXED basis: consensus for Renesas/Melexis/IFX, my scaling of TTM EBITDA for US names. It is indicative only and not used in valuation.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TXN trades at 29.1x CY27 on LSEG $10.10 (29.9x on Zacks $9.84, the same feed as the US peers) and 31.3x NTM, about 40% above the 21.0x peer median. I apply 23.5x to horizon NTM EPS, which is inside the peer range: ~12% above the 21.0x CY27 median, ~6% above the 22.1x US core NTM median, and below ADI (25.0x CY27, 25.9x NTM). In round 1 I wrongly called 24x 'the median': that median included LSCC, POWI and DIOD (1-2 estimates). This set replaces them with IFX, Renesas and Melexis.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A premium of ~10-12%, not 40%, is the most I can argue will persist through Oct 2027. Persistent factors with evidence: (1) structurally higher margins and returns from owned 300mm analog capacity: Q2 2026 gross margin ~61% and ROIC 25.5%, and these hold through cycles because the fab cost advantage is physical; (2) FCF conversion above 100% of earnings through 2028, because depreciation of the new fabs exceeds falling capex and $2.16B of CHIPS receivables remain, all contractually or physically locked in; (3) a 100%-of-FCF return policy and a 7% dividend raise in Sept 2026, with leverage still only ~1x EBITDA after SLAB. Offsets: TXN's CY27 EPS growth (+19% LSEG, +16% Zacks) is the lowest of the 10 peers except Renesas; its cyclicality matches peers; and lean-channel/peaking-sentiment data (ECIA index down 17 points from June) suggest growth momentum, which supports the current multiple, peaks within the horizon. ADI has higher margins and growth and sits at 25x, so TXN should sit between the median and ADI. Sell-side outperform calls are not used.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$208 (-29%) TXN would trade at ~19x horizon NTM EPS of $10.95, or ~20.6x the $10.10 CY27 consensus. That is below the 21x peer median, with the quality premium fully gone. Reaching it in under a year most likely means the shortage has flipped into a destocking cycle (lead times and broker premiums collapsing, distributor book-to-bill below 1, ECIA index falling toward 100, Q1/Q2 2027 guides below seasonal) or China has broken the Nov-2025 truce and imposed analog duties. Ordinary 42% volatility would not usually take it there. It sits just above my $195 bear case.

key_uncertainties: Whether 2026 demand is end demand or restocking/double-ordering. Broker trackers show 60-70 week ADI lead times and TI pricing on open POs, but TI's own lead times are only a couple of weeks above a sub-13-week baseline, TI admitted auto pull-in, and distributor sentiment (ECIA) peaked in June.
Multiple compression: TXN at ~31x NTM vs a 21-22x peer median; even meeting estimates, a move to 23.5x is worth about -10% to fair value.
Thin CY28 consensus (5 estimates) and the SLAB GAAP drag (amortization, integration costs).
Macro: Kalshi prices a 2027 US recession at ~19% (Oct 4 2026, ~557k contracts traded).
China (~22% of revenue) and tariff policy; the anti-dumping probe is dormant under the truce but not visibly closed.
reasoning: Round 2. I took the supervisor's fact corrections: Q2 EPS was $2.14 GAAP, not $2.17; the dividend is $6.08 a year and goes ex Oct 30 inside the 1-month window; TI-defined TTM FCF is $6.53B including $1.18B CHIPS, with $2.16B still to collect; the broader LSEG consensus is CY27 $10.10; the SLAB deal adds ~$7.3B net outlay and is ~neutral to EPS before amortization; the China anti-dumping probe is covered by the Nov-2025 termination commitment. I re-checked consensus and quotes directly (Nasdaq API) and MarketScreener for the non-US peers. New in-lane evidence beyond the Fusion Greensheet that agent 2 shares: (a) ECIA's distributor/manufacturer sentiment index fell from 154.1 in June to 136.7 in August, with growth expected to peak in Q3; (b) Portrait Analytics' channel read says inventory is lean across peers (MCHP 26 days, ADI 6.5 weeks) and TI's DIO fell 13 days to 196, but TI's own lead times are only modestly extended and TI admitted auto pull-in; (c) Avnet's June quarter was +50% y/y with book-to-bill above 1 in every region and inventory days down to 71; (d) a direct Kalshi API read prices a 2027 recession at 19c on ~557k volume, replacing the discounted 2026 tracker figure. Net read: the upcycle is real and the channel is not stuffed, so near-term numbers are safe, but the rate of change is peaking. For analog stocks that is historically when multiples compress. So I dropped my +3.5% EPS uplift as double-counting the upward revisions, and I moved from 'peer median, no premium' at 24x to a disclosed ~12% premium at 23.5x over a reconciled 21.0x median of 10 genuine peers. FCF-yield leg: 4.0% on ~$11.0 FCF/share plus ~$1.1 of post-horizon CHIPS cash. Fair value is $265, down from $293. The ladder is not the fair value: estimate momentum, lean channels and the 25% bull case keep the 12-month median above it, at ~$282 (mean ~$288, plus a $6 dividend). Scenarios: $195 (25%), $283 (50%), $390 (25%). The ladder is a lognormal with median $282 and sigma 0.36, with the left tail fattened by ~1-2 points for a destocking turn. Lane share: 10 of 20 sources are in-lane alt-data/newsletter/prediction-market. Excluding the TI and Avnet filings and consensus feeds used only for basic reported facts and comps, that is about 63%. X/Twitter and Reddit remained unfetchable, and research in this round was limited to ~8 searches/fetches.

revisions.why: The supervisor's comps review showed my 24.1x 'median' was inflated by non-comparables. The reconciled 21.0x median makes 23.5x a disclosed premium. I dropped the +3.5% EPS uplift (double-counting LSEG revisions), added the SLAB GAAP drag (-$0.25) and used 915M shares; the CHIPS remainder partly offsets.
Supervisor findings on the consensus base ($10.10 LSEG), the SLAB amortization effect and the peer median. The ECIA and Portrait evidence argues against the pricing uplift.

Supervisor flagged that CHIPS incentives ($1.18B TTM, $2.16B remaining) were excluded. I add the post-horizon portion as a one-off. I raise the yield to 4.0% so the FCF multiple stays consistent with the reconciled peer P/E. Lower EPS base, 915M shares.
Lower peer median (21x) for bear derating, base multiple compression toward ~25x NTM, and evidence that growth momentum is peaking (ECIA, TI auto pull-in admission).

Lower fair value ($265) and peaking-momentum evidence pull the median ~4% down. Estimate momentum and lean channels keep it above fair value. I disagree with fully converging on $265 because the upcycle is still live (Avnet +50% y/y, book-to-bill > 1).
Ex-dividend $1.52 on Oct 30 inside the window (supervisor). TI's lead times are only modestly up and ECIA sentiment rolled over, so I trimmed the beat drift.
Re-based to ~19x horizon NTM EPS ($10.95), i.e. ~20.6x CY27 $10.10, just below the reconciled 21x peer median, consistent with the lower bear case.
Supervisor discounted the tracker figure. I read the 2027 contract directly.
